notes.mid_cycle: Transaction revenue (61% of Q3 revenue) is cyclical. FY2026 is treated as roughly mid-cycle IN AGGREGATE and not adjusted: options (FY26E ~1,406) and equities (~452) run at record volumes (Q3 equity notional $992B +53%, options 905M contracts +48%) and record margin book ($22.9B Oct), i.e. above mid-cycle, while crypto (~450 vs 901 in 2025 and ~626 in 2024) is near a trough. The two roughly offset (ours). The bear takes the down-cycle on options/equities with crypto staying low.
notes.segments_fy26e: ours from 9M + Q4E: options 1,406; event contracts 613 (9M 433, Q3 173 = 12% of revenue, mostly sports); crypto 450; equities 452; other transaction 201; net interest 1,588 (incl. corporate cash 157; margin interest 9M 652 +73%, sweep 131 -24%, securities lending -5 vs +164, credit card net 122 +205%); other revenue 520 (Gold subscriptions + Trump Account service revenue; Gold subs 5.2M +34%).
notes.growth: Base 2027 +19%: the Q4 run-rate alone (1,395 ex interest x 4 = 5,580) is +9.8% over 2026, plus ~3%/quarter sequential growth from net deposits (LTM $80.5B = 23% of platform assets, Oct release), Gold (+34%), credit card, banking, event contracts annualising; then 15/13/12/11/10%. Below consensus FY2027 revenue 6,881 (+29%, 28 analysts): consensus has been too high on revenue in 3 of the last 4 quarters (Q4-25 1,283 vs 1,341; Q1-26 1,067 vs 1,136; Q2-26 1,308 vs 1,281; Q3-26 1,424 vs 1,433; AV estimates). Bull = consensus in 2027: +32% ex interest (= consensus revenue 6,881 incl. ~170 corporate interest) and a 49% margin, giving EPS ~2.88 vs consensus 2.93 (crypto recovery to the 2025 level, event contracts win in court, perpetual futures / 24-7 equities / international); then 20/17/15/13/11. The revenue beat record does not support a bull above consensus (3 of the last 4 quarters missed); EPS beats (+7% to +41% in 2026) came with one-offs (RVI gain Q2, tax). Bear = company-specific hit: sports event contracts lost in most states (9th and 6th Circuit rulings against, Nevada/Michigan/Ohio exits, SCOTUS cert pending) and federal excise-tax risk, a PFOF challenge more likely after the midterm shift (Trefis 6.11.2026), options/equity volumes fall from records, crypto stays low, rate cuts: 2027 -14% (analog: 2022 revenue -25% after the 2021 boom, 1,815 -> 1,358; today's mix is more diversified: options/equities -25% = -465, event contracts -60% = -370, crypto -20% = -90, net interest -10% = -145 -> about -20% at worst; -14% taken), then 3/8/8/8/7.

FY2025 ~44.6%; 9M26 (1,670-112)/(3,799-112) = 42.3%; Q3-26 46.3%; FY2026E 41.1% (41.5% before the 23M restructuring): opex ran ahead of revenue in 2026 (Trump Accounts, Rothera, credit-card provisions 9M 163 +109%, marketing). Base 43.3% in 2027 (revenue +19% vs opex +15%) rising ~1pt/yr to 47% (peers: SCHW ~45-50% pre-tax, IBKR ~70%+). Bull 49% -> 53% (consensus FY27 EPS 2.93 implies ~50% incl. interest). Bear 36% -> 39%: on revenue -14% (4,370) the 2026 cost base 2,985 cut ~7% (brokerage/transaction and marketing are variable; HOOD cut costs in 2022) gives 36.5%.
